trigger_evals.query: I need to add a small overlay div in the gamified project card — absolute position, inset-0, z-index 4, background set to our minimalist background color. Where should that live, inline or in styles.css?
I'm migrating the old cv-header.module.css to Tailwind, can you help me decide what stays as CSS and what becomes utility classes?
I want to add a new breakpoint for the skill-constellation component, something like 880px for tablet. How should I define that?
This chip component needs a selected state style and also a hover effect — should the hover go in CSS or as a Tailwind variant?
I copy-pasted the same className string with like 8 utility classes into three different card components, is that ok or should I extract it?
Can you review this PR diff and check if the CSS changes follow our project conventions for BEM naming and breakpoints?
Write a TypeScript function that validates a CPF number using regex.
Why is my Next.js build failing with 'Module not found: Can't resolve @/lib/utils'?
Add a new translation key for the project modal's close button in both pt-BR.json and en.json.
Explain how getCmsGraph does the BFS traversal starting at content/index.md.

evals.prompt: I need to add a small overlay inside the project card in the gamified feature. It just needs position: absolute, inset: 0, z-index: 4, and background set to the minimalist background token. Should I write a BEM class in styles.css for this or do it some other way?
evals.expected_output: The skill applies the core test: none of the declarations depend on a media query, pseudo-element, relational selector, @keyframes, or theme/JS-state-dependent custom property, so it recommends inline Tailwind utilities (e.g. absolute inset-0 z-4 bg-minimalist-background) instead of a new BEM rule, and does not invent a new class name for it.

assertions.text: The response recommends inline Tailwind utility classes instead of a new CSS/BEM rule for this block

The response explains the recommendation using the core test (no media query, pseudo-element, relational selector, keyframes, or theme/state-dependent custom property), not just an unexplained style preference
The suggested class uses the project's existing background token (e.g. bg-minimalist-background) rather than an arbitrary color value

evals.prompt: I'm migrating src/features/curriculum/cv-header.module.css to Tailwind utilities. One rule is `.cv-header__badge:hover { transform: scale(1.05); }` and another is `.cv-header { display: flex; gap: 12px; }`. How should I split this between inline classes and styles.css?
evals.expected_output: The skill classifies each declaration individually: `.cv-header` (plain flex/gap, no pseudo-class/media dependency) moves to inline Tailwind utilities (flex gap-3 or similar); the `:hover` rule is flagged as a pseudo-class interaction that should become a native Tailwind hover: variant directly in className rather than staying as a hand-written CSS pseudo-class rule, and never as a manual --hover BEM modifier.

assertions.text: The response treats the two rules separately rather than deciding to migrate or keep the whole block as one unit
The static display:flex / gap rule is moved to inline Tailwind utility classes
The :hover rule is converted to a native Tailwind hover: variant in className, not kept as a CSS :hover selector and not turned into a manual --hover BEM modifier class

evals.prompt: I want to add a tablet breakpoint for the skill-constellation feature, around 880px, so a className can use something like max-tablet: or min-tablet:. How do I set this up correctly in this project?
evals.expected_output: The skill instructs defining a named token in a @theme block (not @theme inline) inside src/features/skill-constellation/styles.css, e.g. --breakpoint-tablet: 880px, checks that the name doesn't collide with another feature's breakpoint tokens (e.g. gamified's --breakpoint-cv), and explicitly forbids an arbitrary literal like max-[880px]: in the className.

assertions.text: The response defines the breakpoint as a @theme token (not @theme inline) with a feature-namespaced name like --breakpoint-tablet
The response mentions checking for name collisions with breakpoint tokens already declared in other features' styles.css files
The response explicitly says not to use an arbitrary breakpoint literal like max-[880px]: or a hardcoded pixel value in @media

evals.prompt: The chip component in src/features/gamified needs two states: a 'selected' state (only exists in React state, not a real CSS pseudo-class) and a hover effect when the user mouses over it. How should each be implemented?
evals.expected_output: The skill recommends the hover effect be a native Tailwind hover: variant directly in className (or inside the CVA definition), and the 'selected' state be a manual BEM modifier (e.g. sc-chip--selected) applied conditionally in JS, since it has no CSS pseudo-class equivalent.

assertions.text: Hover is implemented with the native hover: Tailwind variant, not a hand-maintained --hover modifier class
The 'selected' state is implemented as a manual BEM modifier class (e.g. --selected) since it exists only in JS/React state, not as a CSS pseudo-class

evals.prompt: I've written className="flex items-center gap-2 rounded-full border border-minimalist-border px-3 py-1 text-minimalist-sm" in three separate card components now (ProjectCard, SkillCard, ExperienceCard). Is that fine or should I do something about it?
evals.expected_output: The skill flags this as the duplication case: the same utility string repeated in 2+ components should be extracted into a named constant (a CVA definition or an exported className string), not left copy-pasted across the three components.

assertions.text: The response identifies this as a duplication problem since the same utility string appears in 3 components
The response recommends extracting the className string into a named constant (CVA definition or exported string), not leaving it duplicated

evals.prompt: Can you review this diff? It adds `.sc-row-2 { display:flex; }` to skill-constellation/styles.css and also adds `max-[670px]:hidden` directly in the JSX of the same component.
evals.expected_output: The skill flags two issues: the class name `.sc-row-2` violates BEM naming (abbreviated/non-descriptive element name) and should describe the role of the element; and `max-[670px]:hidden` is an arbitrary breakpoint literal that should instead use a named variant tied to a @theme token (e.g. max-mobile:hidden).

assertions.text: The response flags .sc-row-2 as violating BEM naming conventions (non-descriptive element name) and suggests a descriptive alternative
The response flags max-[670px]: as an arbitrary breakpoint literal and recommends a named variant backed by a @theme token instead

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript function that validates a CPF number using regex.
evals.expected_output: The css-tailwind-decision skill is NOT triggered; this is unrelated code logic with no styling/className involved.
